entries.title: EU Batteries Regulation - Comprehensive Safety, Sustainability and Recycling Requirements
entries.summary: The EU Batteries Regulation covers sourcing, manufacturing, use, and recycling of batteries with comprehensive safety, sustainability, and recycling requirements. It includes 15 ambitious measures supporting the battery sector through significant capital and R&D funding through 2030.

entries.title: EU Minimum Recycled Content Rules and Battery Reusability Standards
entries.summary: New minimum recycled content requirements effective August 18, 2031: 16% cobalt, 85% lead, 6% lithium, and 6% nickel in batteries. Portable batteries must be sealed, weigh ≤5kg, and be easily removable with simple tools for recycling compliance.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation Implementation Phase - Phased Obligations 2025-2030s
entries.summary: As of 2026, the EU Battery Regulation is in full implementation phase with substantive obligations phased between 2025-2028. Requirements span carbon accounting, production obligations, material restrictions, and performance/durability standards for rechargeable industrial and EV batteries.

entries.title: E-Moped Battery Compliance - UNECE R136 and EU Batteries Regulation 2023/1542
entries.summary: L-category vehicle batteries require UNECE R136 type approval and compliance with EU Batteries Regulation 2023/1542 including labeling, durability classifications, and carbon-footprint disclosure. REESS safety tests cover short-circuit, overcharge, vibration, mechanical impact, and fire safety.

entries.title: EU Batteries Regulation Digital Battery Passport and Lifecycle Traceability
entries.summary: The EU Battery Regulation requires digital battery passport, traceability of raw materials, carbon footprint reporting, and lifecycle transparency spanning design, production, transport, use, and recycling. Focuses on safer batteries and responsible supply chains.

entries.title: Lithium Battery Transport Compliance - UN 38.3 Testing and SDS Requirements
entries.summary: Lithium batteries require valid UN 38.3 test reports from accredited labs (ISO/IEC 17025) and compliant Safety Data Sheets citing UN 3480, Class 9. Documentation must be current and match exact battery models for EU customs compliance.

entries.title: Joint Industry Guidance on Battery Manufacturer Definition
entries.summary: EUROBAT, EPBA, and Recharge released joint guidance clarifying manufacturer definition under EU Batteries Regulation with legal interpretation, key duties, and compliance examples supporting consistent application across the battery value chain.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation: Due Diligence Obligations - Enforcement Postponed to August 2027
entries.summary: EU has postponed enforcement of battery due diligence obligations from August 2025 to August 2027. Large companies placing batteries on the EU market must implement due diligence policies, digital traceability systems, supplier risk assessments, grievance mechanisms, and public reporting. Supply chain mapping remains the biggest challenge as most companies lack visibility beyond tier two suppliers.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation Chapter VII - Supply Chain Due Diligence Requirements
entries.summary: Chapter VII of the EU Battery Regulation applies from August 18, 2027, imposing due diligence obligations on economic operators placing batteries on the market. Companies must establish risk-based environmental and human rights due diligence policies for cobalt, natural graphite, lithium, and nickel sourcing for batteries above 2 kWh capacity, and establish UNGP-based grievance mechanisms.

entries.title: EU Battery Passport and Digital Traceability Requirements - February 2027
entries.summary: Starting February 2027, batteries must have a Battery Passport containing lifecycle information including manufacturing data, carbon footprint data, and recycled material content. Supply chain due diligence requirements take effect August 2027, requiring companies to implement systems for responsible sourcing and supply chain transparency.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542 - Lifecycle Regulation and Market Access Requirements
entries.summary: EU Battery Regulation governs batteries across their entire lifecycle from raw material sourcing through manufacturing, market implementation, use-phase performance, to repurposing and recycling. It integrates sustainability metrics, carbon accounting, supply chain due diligence, and digital traceability as direct market access requirements, aligning with Circular Economy Action Plan and climate neutrality objectives.

entries.title: EU Battery Passport Documentation Requirements - Supply Chain Due Diligence Reports
entries.summary: Companies must document supply chain due-diligence reports describing due-diligence policies, risk-management processes, verification activities, and third-party supply chain assurances. EU Taxonomy disclosure statements and sustainability report availability must be provided as part of battery passport requirements.

entries.title: RoHS 2026 Exemption Structure Transformation - Pack 22 Updates
entries.summary: The EU RoHS landscape is undergoing significant structural transformation in 2026, phasing out broad exemptions in favor of narrower, application-specific sub-entries. The European Commission has finalized a strategy to phase out general lead exemptions through granular Pack 22 updates, requiring compliance professionals to manage a rapidly fragmenting list of technical exemptions.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation - Removability and Replaceability Requirements
entries.summary: Article 11 requirements of the EU Battery Regulation enter into force on February 18, 2027, stipulating that portable batteries in appliances must be readily removable and replaceable by end users or independent professionals. The regulation also maintains and updates restrictions on hazardous substances including mercury, cadmium, and lead with new exemptions and review clauses.

entries.title: ECHA February 2026 REACH SVHC Candidate List Update
entries.summary: The European Chemicals Agency published an update to the REACH Candidate List of Substances of Very High Concern (SVHC) on February 4, 2026, adding two new substances for a total of 253 entries. Suppliers must inform downstream users and consumers if an SVHC is present in articles above 0.1% weight by weight and have notification duties to ECHA.

entries.title: RoHS Exemptions - Nine Key Changes and Stricter Limits
entries.summary: Proposed changes affecting nine critical RoHS exemptions include stricter limits on lead in electronic solders, cadmium in batteries, and hexavalent chromium in surface coatings, with shorter duration of exemptions. These changes require manufacturers to prepare for more restrictive material usage and compliance timelines.

entries.title: EU WEEE Directive Review - Circular Economy Act
entries.summary: The European Commission is expected to review the WEEE framework in 2026 as part of the upcoming Circular Economy Act. The WEEE Directive was originally adopted in 2002 and last updated in 2012.

entries.title: WEEE Regulations Amendment 2025 - Online Marketplace Operators
entries.summary: The 2025 WEEE Amendments establish online marketplace operators as producers for EEE supplied by non-UK sellers via their platforms, making marketplaces responsible for WEEE registration and financing. A new vapes category (7.1) has been added to the WEEE classification.

entries.title: 2026 WEEE Overhaul - Extended Producer Responsibility Update
entries.summary: Europe's 2026 WEEE revision represents a complete accountability overhaul for the electronics industry, addressing the 25-point gap between current 40% recovery rates and the 65% target. Cross-border online sales compliance gaps are being addressed through updated frameworks.

entries.title: Swedish WEEE Regulation Implementation
entries.summary: New Swedish WEEE regulations come into force on 12 August 2026, replacing current Swedish regulations. Some provisions will apply at later dates.

entries.title: EU Radio Equipment Directive (RED) - Articles 3.3(d), (e), (f) Cybersecurity Requirements
entries.summary: As of August 1, 2025, Articles 3.3(d), (e), and (f) of the Radio Equipment Directive (RED) are mandatory for wireless-connected devices sold in the EU. These essential cybersecurity requirements apply to all wireless devices from smartphones to IoT equipment requiring CE marking compliance.

entries.summary: EN 18031 series compliance is mandatory for all internet-connected radio equipment placed on EU market since August 1, 2025. The three-part standard covers network protection (EN 18031-1), personal data protection (EN 18031-2), and financial transaction security (EN 18031-3).

entries.summary: EU Regulation 2023/1542, effective February 18, 2024, establishes a comprehensive regulatory framework governing the entire battery lifecycle from production to recycling and disposal. The regulation introduces stringent requirements for production, labeling, and waste treatment with particular focus on lithium battery safety, sustainability, and competitiveness in the EU market.

entries.title: New EU Battery Regulation 2026 - Extended Requirements and Deadlines
entries.summary: The new EU Battery Regulation applies uniformly across all Member States affecting manufacturers, importers, sellers, and consumers. It introduces stricter safety and environmental standards, extended producer responsibility, easier consumer return options, and technical norms for battery durability and reusability, with implementation deadlines stretching from 2024 to 2036.

entries.title: Recycling of Lithium-Ion Batteries & Accumulators - 2025 Compliance
entries.summary: EU Regulation 2023/1542 replaced the outdated 2006 Battery Directive, establishing new obligations for companies manufacturing, importing, distributing, or selling lithium-ion batteries. The regulation addresses regulatory, logistical, and environmental responsibilities related to battery recycling and compliance requirements for 2025.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation: Due Diligence Obligations - Enforcement Postponed to August 2027
entries.summary: The EU has postponed enforcement of battery due diligence obligations from August 2025 to August 2027. Once in force, large companies placing batteries on the EU market must implement due diligence policies, digital traceability systems, supplier risk assessments, grievance mechanisms, and public reporting. Supply chain mapping remains the biggest challenge as most companies lack visibility beyond tier two suppliers.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation: Lifecycle Regulation and Compliance Requirements
entries.summary: The EU Battery Regulation integrates sustainability metrics, carbon accounting, supply chain due diligence, and digital traceability into market access requirements. The regulation governs batteries from raw material sourcing through manufacturing, use-phase performance, to repurposing and recycling, aligning with the Circular Economy Action Plan and climate neutrality objectives.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation Chapter VII: Due Diligence for Batteries - Effective August 18, 2027
entries.summary: Chapter VII of the EU Battery Regulation imposes due diligence obligations on economic operators placing batteries on the market. Companies selling batteries with capacity above 2 kWh must establish risk-based environmental and human rights due diligence policies for cobalt, natural graphite, lithium and nickel, and establish UNGP-based grievance mechanisms.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation: Due Diligence Requires Traceability System
entries.summary: Meeting due diligence obligations under the EU Battery Regulation requires implementation of traceability systems for cobalt, natural graphite, lithium, and nickel supply chains. Economic operators must implement systems to prove provenance and material provenance to satisfy regulatory requirements.

entries.title: European Battery Regulation: Lifecycle Governance and Traceability
entries.summary: The EU Battery Regulation implements lifecycle governance addressing battery reuse, repurposing, traceability, and producer responsibility. Regulatory requirements including battery passports, sustainability due diligence obligations, and extended producer responsibility schemes shape the technical feasibility and market structure of battery applications.

entries.title: EU Sustainable Batteries Regulation: ESG Compliance Guide
entries.summary: Guidance on establishing chain of custody/traceability systems identifying upstream supply chain actors with prescribed information on raw materials, supplier details, and country of origin. Requires incorporation of battery due diligence policies into supply agreements and establishment of UNGP-based grievance mechanisms.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation: Comprehensive Lifecycle Requirements
entries.summary: The EU Battery Regulation effective August 2023 requires manufacturers to meet sustainability requirements across entire battery lifecycle from raw material procurement to disposal and recycling. Manufacturers must report carbon footprint, recycled material use rates, and human rights and environmental due diligence information for active materials.

entries.title: RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU and Commission Delegate Directive (EU) 2015/863
entries.summary: EU directive restricting the use of lead, mercury, cadmium, chromium VI, PBBs, and PBDEs in electrical and electronic equipment. Came into force in July 2011 and replaced the previous 2006/95/EC directive. Establishes maximum concentration limits for hazardous substances in EEE.

entries.title: RoHS 3 Amendment - Phthalates Addition and Exemption Reviews
entries.summary: RoHS 3 added four phthalates (DEHP, BBP, DBP, DIBP) to the list of restricted substances in electrical and electronic equipment. Each substance has specific maximum concentration thresholds (0.1% by weight for most substances, 0.01% for cadmium). The regulatory landscape continues to evolve with ongoing exemption assessments.

entries.title: Chemicals Management for Electronics Regulatory Summit Europe 2026
entries.summary: Industry summit addressing convergence of EU regulatory requirements including RoHS updates, exemption outlook, PFAS restrictions, circular economy implementation, and digital product passports. Scheduled for Brussels & Virtual on 23 April 2026 with regulators, industry leaders, and technical experts.

entries.title: RoHS Compliance Requirements - Exemption Expiration and Supply Chain Impact
entries.summary: RoHS exemptions are expiring and manufacturers must proactively ensure compliance by reviewing Bills of Materials, verifying supplier declarations, and checking technical data sheets. Lead (Pb) must not exceed 0.1% by weight unless specific exemptions apply. Supply chain-wide compliance verification is essential.

entries.title: RoHS Exemptions - Major Changes and Revisions
entries.summary: EU is considering major revisions to key RoHS exemptions that could significantly impact manufacturers of electronic equipment. Proposed changes may affect established compliance strategies for hazardous substance restrictions including lead and cadmium.

entries.title: Europe's WEEE Revision: 2026 Overhaul
entries.summary: EU's upcoming WEEE revision represents a complete accountability overhaul for the electronics industry, addressing the 25-point gap between current 40% recovery rates and the 65% target. The revision addresses compliance gaps from cross-border online sales and outdated frameworks that cannot adequately handle electronic waste management.

entries.title: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (Amendment, etc.) Regulations 2025

entries.summary: EU regulation mandating USB-C as the common charging standard for laptops effective 28 April 2026. Applies to all laptops sold in the EU market.

entries.title: EU Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) - Digital Product Passport
entries.summary: ESPR effective January 2026 mandates that all accessories sold in the European Economic Area must publish a Digital Product Passport (DPP) including material traceability and repairability information.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation - Easy Replacement Requirements
entries.summary: From 18 February 2027, electronic devices sold in the EU must have batteries that can be easily replaced by consumers. Extends product lifespan and supports circular economy principles.

entries.title: Council of the European Union eases rules on replacing damaged charging cables - New Measuring Instruments Directive
entries.summary: The new measuring instruments directive establishes common standards for electric chargers and gas dispensers, facilitating widespread deployment of charging infrastructure across Europe. This regulation supports the EU's transition to energy-efficient mobility and cleaner energy systems.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542 - Sustainability, Recycling and Carbon Footprint Requirements
entries.summary: Regulation EU 2023/1542 establishes a transformative regulatory framework replacing Directive 2006/66/EC with new sustainability and recycling requirements. entries.title: EU Batteries Regulation 2023/1542 - Stricter Labelling and Collection Targets Coming into Force 2026

The regulation sets higher collection targets (73% for portable batteries by 2030) and recycling efficiency targets (90% for key metals, 50% for lithium by 2027).

entries.summary: FAA released updated guidance on GPS and GNSS interference focusing on jamming and spoofing trends, impacts on aircraft systems, and pilot training recommendations. Addresses growing concern over deliberate GNSS interference affecting commercial aviation.

entries.title: GNSS Resilience Priority - European Commission Response to Interference Crisis
entries.summary: GNSS interference now affects over 5% of commercial flights in Europe with 220% increase in signal-loss events between 2021-2024. Recent malicious interference incidents highlight urgent need for GNSS resilience as economic and security priority for EU markets.

entries.title: GNSS Disruption Impact on European Airspace and Aircraft Systems
entries.summary: Sustained GNSS interference across Europe creates persistent carryover effects in aircraft systems. Spoofing events cause aircraft to operate in corrupted internal states even after exiting interference zones, creating ongoing operational risks.

entries.summary: EU Radio Equipment Directive now mandates cybersecurity compliance through EN 18031 harmonised standards for all connected devices using radio technologies (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, Zigbee, LoRa). Compliance became effective from 2025 and is now an essential requirement for CE marking.

entries.title: EN 18031 Compliance: 2026 Guide for Connected Products
entries.summary: EN 18031 series (three standards covering network protection, personal data protection, and financial transaction security) became mandatory for all new internet-connected radio equipment on EU market since August 1, 2025. Applies to industrial sensors, smart home devices, IoT gateways, wearables, and Zigbee devices.

entries.title: EU Harmonizes Cybersecurity Standards for Radio Equipment Under EN 18031 Series
entries.summary: Three EN 18031 standards (2024 versions) address network functionality protection, personal data/privacy protection, and fraud prevention for virtual currency transactions. Standards were officially listed in EU Official Journal on January 30, 2025, with August 1, 2025 deadline for manufacturer compliance.

entries.title: EN 18031 – Cybersecurity Standard for Radio Equipment
entries.summary: EN 18031 establishes baseline cybersecurity protections for internet-connected radio equipment across three parts: general requirements, personal data protection, and financial security. Standard applies across all industries using wireless/connected devices.

entries.title: Radio Equipment Directive Cybersecurity Testing – EN 18031
entries.summary: BSI guidance on EN 18031 cybersecurity testing requirements for radio equipment including vehicle telematics, Wi-Fi routers, Bluetooth devices, smart wearables, and baby monitors. Specifies exemptions for non-connected radio equipment.

entries.title: EN 18031 Cybersecurity Testing for the Radio Equipment Directive (RED)
entries.summary: Delegated Regulation 2022/30/EU under RED establishes cybersecurity requirements for radio devices effective August 1, 2025. All EU manufacturers of connected radio equipment must ensure devices are protected against network threats, privacy violations, and fraud.

entries.title: Radio Equipment Directive Compliance Requirements
entries.summary: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 on RED became active August 1, 2025, requiring all radio equipment including IoT devices, wearables, and smart toys to comply with cybersecurity requirements through EN 18031-1/2/3 standards. Non-compliance risks fines and product recalls.

entries.title: EN 18031 Cybersecurity Testing for CE Radio Equipment under RED
entries.summary: Since August 2025, cybersecurity is mandatory for CE marking of internet-connected radio equipment under Articles 3(3)(d/e/f) of RED. Requirements address network protection, user privacy, and fraud prevention with focus on authentication mechanisms and device verification.

entries.title: EN 18031 – Cybersecurity Testing of Radio Equipment
entries.summary: From August 1, 2025, all affected radio equipment must meet EN 18031-x requirements to be sold on European market. Timely implementation of new safety standards is essential for market compliance and continued product sales.

entries.title: RED 3.3: Cybersecurity Update to EU Radio Equipment Directive
entries.summary: RED was updated to include cybersecurity requirements under Article 3.3, marking a major step in EU's digital product regulation. This cybersecurity update affects almost every connected product on the market and is accompanied by the Cyber Resilience Act and Digital Product Passport requirements.

entries.title: RED Directive: Cybersecurity Requirements for 4G/5G Radio Equipment
entries.summary: RED Directive now requires security-by-design measures for radio equipment with sensitive functions and mandates appropriate data protection mechanisms such as encrypted communications. These requirements directly apply to 4G/5G repeaters deployed in professional and industrial environments.

entries.title: EU Radio Equipment Directive (RED) 2025 - Revised Harmonized Standards
entries.summary: The European Commission published Implementation Decision (EU) 2025/2499 revising RED harmonized standards for short-range devices and airborne mobile communication systems. This update reflects the latest regulatory evolution for radio equipment compliance in the EU.

entries.title: EU Radio Equipment Directive (CE-RED) Certification Requirements and Costs
entries.summary: Cellular and mobile devices with 4G/LTE/5G must comply with EN 301 EMC standards and other EN standards for radio equipment. RED lab testing is mandatory to verify product compliance before entering the EU market.

entries.title: Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) - Cybersecurity Requirements for Connected Devices
